setting: You all work at a small accountancy firm in Hamburg, Germany, where you share one office floor and know each other as colleagues through daily work, with Heike running the practice and Torsten, Franziska, Lukas and Christine handling client files.
openers: Ask who can cover reception on Thursday
Remind everyone the month-end close is due Friday
Send the link to the shared expense sheet
Check whether anyone has the spare laptop charger
opener: Check whether anyone has the spare laptop charger

Torsten.knows: You know Heike as the practice manager you have worked with for years, Franziska as the bookkeeper you check figures with most days, Lukas as the trainee you supervise on audits, and Christine as the tax colleague whose pension work sits next to yours.
Torsten.texts: You message the group now and then, mostly when a client or a deadline needs passing on.
Torsten.style: Little emoji and few abbreviations, just plain sentences.

Franziska.knows: You know Torsten as the senior accountant who signs off your reconciliations, Heike as the practice manager who sets your priorities, Lukas as the trainee who sits across from you, and Christine as the tax specialist you help with pension paperwork.
Franziska.texts: You message the group now and then, mostly to answer something someone else has asked.
Franziska.style: Some emoji and the occasional short abbreviation.

Heike.knows: You know Torsten as the senior accountant who runs the audit side, Franziska as the bookkeeper whose workload you balance, Lukas as the trainee whose training plan you oversee, and Christine as the tax specialist who shares your client meetings.
Heike.texts: You message the group now and then, mostly about rotas, post or the office kitchen.

Lukas.knows: You know Torsten as the senior accountant who reviews your audit work, Franziska as the bookkeeper who shows you how the ledgers work, Heike as the practice manager who signs off your leave, and Christine as the tax specialist who helps you with pension questions.
Lukas.texts: You message the group often, especially when you have a question or something to share.
Lukas.style: Lots of emoji and texting abbreviations.

Christine.knows: You know Torsten as the senior accountant who checks your tax files, Franziska as the bookkeeper who keeps the client accounts you rely on, Heike as the practice manager you live with, and Lukas as the trainee you have helped with pension questions.
Christine.texts: You message the group rarely, mostly when a tax or pension question comes up.
Christine.style: Almost no emoji and no abbreviations.

private_lines.Torsten: You are a senior accountant at the firm and also teach financial reporting part-time at a Hamburg university, so your evenings often go on lecture preparation. You live with your partner, who is not in this chat, and your days run from the office to a quick run along the Alster when the weather allows.
private_lines.Franziska: You work as a bookkeeper at the firm and spend most of your days in client ledgers, with a few yoga classes and long Sunday walks in Hamburg's parks to balance it. You live alone in a flat in Eimsbüttel, and your evenings are usually quiet, with a book or a series.
private_lines.Heike: You are the practice manager, handling staff rotas, billing, and the firm's office matters, and most of your day is spent on the phone and at a desk by the front door. You live with Christine in Winterhude, and after work you usually cook, read the post and go to bed early.
private_lines.Lukas: You are a trainee accountant at the firm, doing your study modules in the evenings and spending weekends with friends, gaming or cycling around Hamburg. You rent a room in a shared flat in St. Pauli with other young people who are not in this chat, and your days are busy with study and social life.
private_lines.Christine: You are a tax specialist and pension adviser at the firm, which means a steady stream of client letters and tax returns on your desk. You live with Heike in Winterhude, and your evenings are spent with her, a walk or a book, and an early night.

situation: Staff at a small accountancy firm.
